note: Cross-repo contract for the marketplace hire (web WP-37/WP-38/WP-51, app WP-38/WP-51). This file is duplicated byte-for-byte in work-address/web (api/src/test/fixture) and work-address/app (api/src/test/fixture); they are separate repositories, so each owns a copy. web asserts HireClient PRODUCES these bytes, this header and this signature; app asserts its MarketplaceHireDto re-serialises to exactly them and that the controller ACCEPTS them. The body is an accepted offer as the marketplace pushes it: rateHour is whole USDT an hour (0 for fixed-price work), weeklyLimit the hour cap the freelancer accepted (null when the offer set none), weekStartsAt the unix second the contract's first week opens - its start date, or the moment the offer was accepted - so app measures that cap against the same seven days the contract card shows hours for, trackScreenshots and trackProcesses the monitoring those same terms disclosed. app applies all of them to the project it opens rather than its own defaults. freelancerAddress is the fallback for a freelancer with no account there yet (null otherwise); text is the agreed scope. issuedAt (unix seconds) and nonce are the replay guard, as for the settlement push. The HMAC-SHA256 hex signature over the exact serialised bytes goes in the header named below, with the shared entitlement secret. Every key is always present, in this order, because app verifies the signature over its own re-serialisation of the parsed DTO. Change both copies in the same pull request or not at all. ROUTE BINDING: every internal route shares one secret, so the signature names the route it was made for. `signature` is the header value, `v2=<hex>`: HMAC-SHA256 with the shared secret over `signedBytes` - the version, `method`, `path`, the header name in lower case and then `serialised`, joined by single newlines - so these bytes signed for this route are refused on every other. `legacySignature` is the form used before the binding, the bare hex HMAC of `serialised` alone: app accepts it only while APP_INTERNAL_SIGNATURE_ACCEPT_LEGACY is on, web sends it only as the fallback after a 401 while APP_INTERNAL_SIGNATURE_LEGACY_FALLBACK is on, and both go when that one-release window closes (docs/internal-signature.md in each repository).
